note: Codex writes true JSONL, one {timestamp, type, payload} per line. The line's `type` is a container, so it does not identify the record on its own: `response_item` and `event_msg` both carry a second, type-discriminated union in `payload`, and a `message` payload carries a third in `content`. recordTypes therefore decides the five LINE types, and contentBlocks decides all 29 type-discriminated payloads beneath them, the payload unions and the message content blocks alike. Every name across those three levels is distinct, so a lookup is unambiguous; a reader looks up the line type, then the payload type, and both must be decided or the record refuses. Nothing here is derived from, mapped onto, or named after another agent's vocabulary: `function_call` is not `tool_use`, `reasoning` is not `thinking`, and a consumer who wants them unified is the one who gets to decide that. Codex has no equivalent of Claude Code's attachment or system-subtype vocabularies, so those two keys are absent rather than empty.

recordTypes.keep: the line is carried; for the two container types, the payload's own decision governs what survives inside it

rationale.recordTypes.response_item: 8865 lines. A container: the decision only means the reader descends into payload.type, which carries the real decision.
rationale.recordTypes.event_msg: 6627 lines. The same container role as response_item, over a different union. Codex writes the agent's reasoning through BOTH: 1016 `reasoning` summary entries as response_items and 1016 `agent_reasoning` events carry the same prose, 532053 and 495931 bytes. Both are kept; deduplicating them would be deident deciding something the consumer can decide better.
rationale.recordTypes.turn_context: 159 lines, 3301591 bytes, the fifth heaviest type in the corpus. Holds cwd, trace_id, model, personality, a full collaboration-mode developer_instructions block that is vendor boilerplate, and `timezone`. The timezone is the reason this is not a close call: it read Asia/Tokyo, and quantise() spends the entire timestamp budget removing exactly that class of correlation. Shipping the zone as a literal string hands back what the quantisation was for.
rationale.recordTypes.session_meta: 60 lines, one per session, 1219880 bytes. Session id, cwd carrying the account name in its home path, originator, cli_version, model_provider, and base_instructions.text, the whole Codex system prompt, near-identical across all 60 sessions. Identifiers plus vendor boilerplate, with no turn of the conversation in it.
rationale.recordTypes.compacted: 3 lines, 84088 bytes. The name reads as a marker and is not one: `replacement_history` nests a full message list, and the ones measured held the user's original prompts verbatim as input_text blocks, not a summary of them. Kept because it carries user prose. It is also the one kept record that nests other records, so a reader must descend into replacement_history and apply the block decisions there; keeping the line without descending ships unredacted user text.
rationale.contentBlocks.message: 783 payloads, 4618731 bytes. Roles measured: user 242, assistant 471, developer 70. The developer role is injected instruction text riding in as input_text, which is a reader's problem to strip, not a reason to drop the union.
rationale.contentBlocks.function_call: 2821 payloads, 854969 bytes of `arguments`. The agent's chosen action and its parameters; update_plan arguments carry written explanations and plan steps. Names measured: shell_command 1273, exec_command 685, mcp__sequential_thinking__sequentialthinking 158, update_plan 156, spawn_agent 42.
rationale.contentBlocks.function_call_output: 2820 payloads, 13680403 bytes, the single heaviest type in the corpus and near a fifth of it. Tool output, read by the model and by nobody else. shape-only for the reason docs/limits.md gives on the Claude Code side: nothing is kept to truncate, so no cap has to be set generously.
rationale.contentBlocks.reasoning: 1904 payloads. The Claude Code precedent does NOT transfer, and this was checked rather than assumed: Claude Code writes thinking as an empty string and keeps only a signature, 7771 blocks measured empty at 0 bytes. Codex writes real prose. `content` is null in all 1904 and `encrypted_content` is the literal string REDACTED in all 1904 (the dataset's scrub, not Codex's), but `summary` carries 1016 summary_text entries totalling 532053 bytes of agent reasoning. Kept, and the byte cost is real.
rationale.contentBlocks.custom_tool_call: 230 payloads, 553166 bytes, `name` is apply_patch in all 230. `input` is the full apply_patch envelope including the diff body. This is where the agent's authored change actually lives, which is why patch_apply_end can be spent.
rationale.contentBlocks.custom_tool_call_output: 230 payloads, 87437 bytes. The apply_patch result envelope: a success string listing absolute paths, plus exit_code and duration.
rationale.contentBlocks.ghost_snapshot: 73 payloads, 55442 bytes. The name suggests file content and it was checked: there is none. The payload is a git commit id, its parent, and preexisting_untracked_files, up to 135 FILE NAMES in a single snapshot. That is the attachmentTypes.directory situation on the Claude Code side, project vocabulary in its most concentrated form, and it is dropped for the same reason: a file listing identifies a codebase and a client faster than most prose does.
rationale.contentBlocks.web_search_call: 4 payloads, 751 bytes. A status enum plus, on two of the four, an action.url that was opened. A URL and an enum, no prose.
rationale.contentBlocks.token_count: 2273 payloads, 1197483 bytes. Input, cached, output and reasoning token counters plus the context window. Counters only.
rationale.contentBlocks.exec_command_end: 1662 payloads, 6171299 bytes, of which aggregated_output alone is 4578670 across 18 distinct working directories; largest single output 10028 bytes. It carries command, cwd, stdout, stderr, aggregated_output and formatted_output, so yes, it carries command output, and it is the third heaviest type in the corpus. The command line and the exit code are the part a reader reads; the output is not.
rationale.contentBlocks.agent_reasoning: 1016 payloads, 495931 bytes of `text`, none of them empty. Real agent prose, checked rather than assumed against the Claude Code empty-thinking precedent.
rationale.contentBlocks.mcp_tool_call_end: 469 payloads, 7109839 bytes, the second heaviest type. This one record holds BOTH halves of an MCP round trip: `invocation` with server, tool and arguments, and `result`. The arguments are sometimes prose, sequentialthinking ships a written `thought` in them, but the record is dominated by result, and Codex chose not to split the call from the output the way it splits function_call from function_call_output. Decided on that shape: a record that is mostly tool output is shape-only, and the prose riding in the arguments is the price of Codex's own merge. Splitting it into a kept half and a discarded half would be deident reshaping a record, which it does not do.
rationale.contentBlocks.agent_message: 419 payloads, 332020 bytes. The agent's message to the user.
rationale.contentBlocks.patch_apply_end: 219 payloads, 531932 bytes. It does carry the diff, and more than the diff: 218 update, 17 add and 4 delete change entries, and the 21 add and delete entries carry whole file bodies in `content`, 97760 bytes of them. It is still spent, because it is a duplicate: all 219 call_ids also appear on a custom_tool_call, and on 200 of the 219 the added lines are present verbatim in that call's input. The authored change is kept once, at custom_tool_call. What is left here beyond the duplicate is a stdout block listing absolute paths under the account's home directory.
rationale.contentBlocks.task_started: 165 payloads, 34320 bytes. turn_id, model_context_window, and a collaboration-mode enum.
rationale.contentBlocks.user_message: 161 payloads, 125668 bytes. The user's own prose, and the highest-value type in the corpus. Also carries text_elements, which are byte ranges into that prose.
rationale.contentBlocks.task_complete: 119 payloads, 147145 bytes. `last_agent_message` is the agent's closing summary of the turn.
rationale.contentBlocks.collab_waiting_end: 35 payloads, 7455 bytes. Thread ids and a `statuses` object that was empty in all 35 measured. A marker.
rationale.contentBlocks.collab_agent_spawn_end: 34 payloads, 27165 bytes. Carries `prompt`: the instructions the orchestrating agent wrote for a subagent, in prose, with absolute paths in it. Subagent transcripts are not exported, so this and collab_close_end are the only place that delegation is visible at all.
rationale.contentBlocks.collab_close_end: 22 payloads, 52395 bytes. `status.completed` carries what the subagent wrote back; 14 of the 22 hold prose longer than a marker.
rationale.contentBlocks.entered_review_mode: 9 payloads, 1584 bytes. A target enum plus a fixed user_facing_hint such as "current changes".
rationale.contentBlocks.exited_review_mode: 9 payloads, 11538 bytes. `review_output` holds findings with written titles, bodies and an overall_explanation: agent prose, and the substance of a review turn.
rationale.contentBlocks.turn_aborted: 4 payloads, 660 bytes. turn_id plus a reason enum.
rationale.contentBlocks.web_search_end: 4 payloads, 1140 bytes. Kept on the field's nature rather than on the sample, and the sample is stated so the decision can be revisited: `query` held a URL twice and an empty string twice, so no prose was actually observed. A search query is authored intent and closer to a turn than to bookkeeping, and the whole type weighs 1140 bytes. If a later corpus shows the field is only ever a URL, this is the decision to reverse.
rationale.contentBlocks.context_compacted: 3 payloads, 294 bytes. A bare marker carrying nothing but its own type. The compaction's actual content is the `compacted` LINE type, which is a different name and is kept.
rationale.contentBlocks.view_image_tool_call: 1 payload, 225 bytes. A call_id and an absolute path; the one measured named a screenshot under the account's Documents folder, with a date and time in the filename. That is the pdf_reference situation on the Claude Code side: a path is an identifier, and a screenshot filename is often a dated one.
rationale.contentBlocks.input_text: 599 blocks inside `message` payloads. The user's text and the developer role's.
rationale.contentBlocks.output_text: 471 blocks inside `message` payloads. The assistant's text.
